notes: Perfect agreement on sensor development claims (C3, C40-C43). Both evaluators affirm the quantitative characterization and successful optimization of four new iDrugSnFRs with no concerns raised.

Strong agreement on crystallographic structures and candle snuffer mechanism (C4, C29-C36, C37-C39, C107-C109). LLM notes ambiguity in nicotine localization; peer reviewers call this 'potentially a major advance' without raising concerns about structural quality.

Both support the candle snuffer mechanism (C37-C39, C107-C109). LLM provides detailed structural analysis with some caveats about inferential aspects; peer review accepts mechanism without critique as part of crystallography findings.

Perfect agreement on specificity characterization (C44-C51). Both accept the comprehensive testing against agonist panels and the 250-fold selectivity metric, with no concerns about sensor promiscuity.
Perfect agreement on ITC thermodynamic characterization (C52-C57). Both accept the binding affinity measurements and thermodynamic parameters without methodological concerns.

Perfect agreement on stopped-flow kinetics (C58-C63). Both accept the complex binding behavior and non-pseudo-first-order kinetics. LLM notes limitations in extracting kon/koff; peer review accepts as part of overall kinetics characterization.

Perfect agreement on microperfusion kinetics at plasma membrane (C64-C73). Both affirm the millisecond temporal resolution and quantitative characterization, including biphasic decay for some ligands.

Perfect agreement on mammalian cell validation (C5, C74-C85). Both affirm functionality in HeLa cells and neurons with subcellular resolution at PM and ER. Peer reviewers explicitly praise utility in these contexts.

Strong overlap on membrane permeation measurements (C74-C85). LLM emphasizes >30-fold differential crossing rates; peer review accepts ability to track drugs in subcellular compartments with fast time resolution.

Partial overlap on differential permeation (C7, C86-C87, C96, C114). Both support the core finding. LLM provides detailed quantitative analysis; peer review implicitly accepts as part of overall characterization.

Disagreement on logD correlation (C91-C95, C97, C114). LLM expresses uncertainty due to computational algorithm variability and inconsistent correlations. Peer reviewers accept without critique and call work 'potentially a major advance.'

Agreement on novelty of time-resolved measurements for low-permeability drugs (C88-C90). Both accept this as a technical advance, though LLM focuses on novelty claim while peer review emphasizes broader impact.

Disagreement on drug development implications (C115-C118). LLM considers these speculative without in vivo validation; peer reviewers accept discussion and only request broadening beyond nicotine addiction, not correction.
Minor overlap on novelty (C96). Both support the technical advance of measuring membrane permeation for poorly permeable drugs.
Peer review evaluated background claims about smoking cessation drugs (C1-C2, C8-C21) that LLM did not separately assess. Peer reviewers accepted these without challenge.
Peer review evaluated methodological advantages and sensitivity claims (C99-C101) that LLM did not separately assess. Peer reviewers implicitly accepted these as part of overall praise for the tools.
